messages.text: I have a question
I'm here, go ahead.
do you stil have my ticket on the machine we talked about the other day?

Yes, Randall, the tax exemption question is still with the team and your BS-4 cart link from the other day is still live.

Nothing has changed on your side in the meantime. If the link has gone stale when you go to use it, say the word and I'll build you a fresh one.
If I have a string of smaller TH miners running, will they have the same effect as having one big machine?

For pool mining, yes, near enough. Three 6 TH/s units and one 18 TH/s unit hash the same, and the pool pays on total hashrate either way. Same for solo odds.

The differences are practical. Small units use more watts per TH, so your power bill is higher for the same hashrate. You also get three power supplies, three lots of fan noise, and three things that can fail.

Buying one at a time to spread the cost is a fair reason to go small, though.
I want a machine that will produce money consistantly
Ran the power-cost calculator
Read the magic miner 40t page
Read the bsb b30 page
Searched the catalog · Magic Miner 40T Harlo B30 miner

Straight with you: no home miner "produces money consistently" at retail power rates. Pool mining gives steady small payouts, but once you subtract the electricity, most of these are close to break-even. It's stacking sats plus a lottery shot, not income.

If consistent payouts are the goal, more hashrate per watt is what matters. The Magic Miner 40T is the best value we sell, $799 for 40 TH/s, versus $599.99 for 18 TH/s on the BS-4. The B30 is $899 for 30 TH/s but sips power in ECO mode.

What's your power rate in Kansas?
11cents

11 cents is decent, that helps. Here's the monthly power cost at your rate, running 24/7:

Magic Miner 40T, 650W standard, about $52 a month for 40 TH/s. In Eco, 450W for 30 TH/s, about $36.

Harlo B30, 485W turbo for 30 TH/s, about $39. In ECO, 230W for 18 TH/s, about $18.

BS-4, 300W for 18 TH/s, about $24.

Note the B30 in ECO does the same 18 TH/s as the BS-4 for less power. That's the efficiency difference you pay for up front.

Mining revenue I won't guess at, it moves with BTC price and difficulty.
I'm leaning toward the magic miner but am looking at the power consumption and working on a break on the electricy

Good instinct. The 40T has three modes in the dashboard, so you control that: Eco at 450W gives you 30 TH/s for about $36 a month, standard 650W gives 40 TH/s for about $52. Skip Turbo, it voids the warranty.

Running Eco most of the time and standard when rates are off-peak is what a lot of people do.

One thing to know: the 40T is a pre-sale, current listing is Batch 8. Want me to confirm the exact ship date on that batch before you decide?
yes
Looked something up in Shopify

Got it: Batch 8 ships December 7, 2026 for a US address. 24 of the 50 units in that batch are still open.

So it's a wait. If you'd rather have something hashing sooner, the BS-4 in your cart ships now at 18 TH/s. If the 40 TH/s at $19.98 per terahash is what you want, the 40T is worth the wait and nothing else on a desk comes close on price per TH.

Want me to build you a cart for the 40T?
sure
Built a cart

Here you go, one Magic Miner 40T at $799, Batch 8:

····

Ships December 7, 2026. Shipping and Kansas tax get added when you put your address in, and the power supply is built in, so it's the unit, a standard IEC cord and your WiFi.

Your BS-4 link still works too if you want both open while you decide.
Is there a discount offer if I buy two
Handed to the team · discount request, not mine to give

Prices are as listed, so I can't set one myself. I've put the question to Georges, and he can jump into this chat and answer on the two-unit side.

Stay in the chat if you can, and if you step away he'll come back to you by email.

Worth knowing on the power side: two 40Ts in Eco is 900W, about $72 a month at your rate. That's a real jump from one.
I know but twice the th power

Fair point, and it does scale cleanly: 60 TH/s in Eco, 80 in standard, no efficiency penalty for running two.

Two things to plan for. Power: 1,300W at standard is most of a 15A household circuit, so put them on separate circuits if you run them hard. Heat and noise roughly double, two units at 50 dB in the same room is noticeable.

Batch 8 has 24 units left, so two is no problem. Want me to make the cart a quantity of two while Georges looks at your question?
Give me a few days to consider it

Of course, take your time. Both cart links stay live, and Georges will come back on the two-unit question either here or by email.

One thing to keep in mind: Batch 8 units sell down, so the cart doesn't hold a unit for you.

While you're thinking, one question I'm curious about: is the plan to run these somewhere in the house, or do you have a garage or shop in mind? That changes the noise and heat answer a fair bit.
I'm thinking of setting them up in my ship

I'll take that as your shop, but tell me if you actually mean a boat, because that changes the answer.

A shop is a good spot: noise stops mattering and the heat is a bonus in winter. Two things to watch, dust, since the fans pull air through a heatsink and a dirty shop clogs it, and winter temperature if it's unheated. They prefer above freezing.

If you did mean a boat, the PSU runs 100 to 240V on an IEC cord, so shore power is fine but inverter-only is a lot of draw.
shop

Good, that's the easy case then. Get them off the floor on a bench or shelf so they're not breathing sawdust, and blow the heatsink out with compressed air every month or two.

Power wise, a shop usually has better circuits than a house, so running both at standard is more realistic out there.

They'll need WiFi reach or an ethernet run, the 40T takes both. Worth checking your signal out there before December.
I have an extender in my shop

That'll do it. Mining uses almost no bandwidth, it just needs the connection to stay up, so an extender is fine.

The 40T does both 2.4 and 5 GHz, so you're not stuck on the 2.4 band like some of the smaller miners. If the extender ever drops, the unit has an ethernet port as a backup.

That's the setup sorted then. Take your few days, and Georges will come back on the two-unit question.
Does the fortun bs-4 use the 2.4 bandwith only
Searched the catalog · Bitfortun BS-4

Yes, the BS-4 is 2.4 GHz WiFi only, plus an ethernet port.

Not a problem with an extender as long as it broadcasts a 2.4 GHz band, most do. If yours is 5 GHz only, you'd be on ethernet.

One correction while I'm looking at the listing: the BS-4 is water cooled, and the power supply is an external Mean Well LRS-350 brick, not built in like the 40T.
I have both

Then you're covered either way, both units will connect without a fuss.

Nothing left blocking you except the two-unit question with Georges and the tax exemption. Take your few days, both cart links stay live.
ok

Sounds good, Randall. Come back whenever and I'll pick it up where we left off.
